Odin × Godot

Kit World protocol v2

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Normal traffic and confirmationReceipt feedback and caller timingActions, proof and cleanup

Status: the cleaned implementation passes eight focused World groups, four caller groups, a real32-body Core/SDK short pair and the primary impaired 600-second Kit policy. Remaining Gate B matrix and CPU validation are open.

The normal World route must not depend on a reliable full checkpoint every three ticks. Its roughly 130 KB checkpoints produced about 2.6 MB/s per client and made confirmation wait for bulk reconstruction. This revision replaces that normal traffic with accepted inputs and complete canonical signatures. Replay and the shared Box3D solver are separate and remain unchanged.

Normal traffic and confirmation#

  • Bump WORLD_NETWORK_REV and the input-catalog identity to v2. Reject old peers explicitly; do not reinterpret v1 packets.
  • Keep client INPUT batches bounded to the existing eight-tick redundancy window. Bind them to the actual player's current validated bootstrap scope.
  • Send small authoritative ACCEPTED batches reliably, including their bounded receipt-feedback entries. Keeping accepted decisions ordered and delivered is affordable once bulk state leaves the normal stream.
  • At the existing three-tick cadence, send a small reliable SIGNATURE message containing the existing complete bd.Signature. It covers identity, epoch, tick and all five canonical parts: Solver, Game, Side, Observations and Occurrences. The Game part includes the canonical accepted-input window.
  • Welcome, Reset and mismatch recovery retain complete canonical states. Explicit diagnostic checkpoint APIs remain distinguishable from normal transport; automatic normal full Correction broadcasts stop.

Receiving a signature is not permission to advance confirmation. The client must have every accepted driver for every tick from its confirmed frontier through T, the canonical accepted prefix needed to sign T, and a locally simulated frame T. Missing data stays pending or requests bounded recovery; Held/Unknown predictions cannot fill a gap in authoritative evidence.

Reuse world_operation staging and pre-publication verification. When accepted values require repair, verify the staged frame T before publishing. When the local state already agrees, a confirmation transaction must still verify before advancing its frontier. Catch-up uses real accepted-input simulation, within eight ticks, rather than a ticker assignment. On mismatch, preserve the last confirmed publication and use the existing Reset request path. Confirmation must not replay already confirmed effects.

World_Frame currently stores no canonical signature. The existing signer encodes the complete parts and produces a 480-byte signature. Compute at the declared cadence; do not introduce an invalid cache over mutable accepted metadata or claim that signing is free. Measure the resulting operation.

Receipt feedback and caller timing#

Authority feedback reports the newest fully validated class0 proposal received from each actual player. It is distinct from the tick accepted by the authority. Validate every typed row, sender, schema, epoch, scope, sequence and trailing byte before changing receipt state. A valid late receipt can inform timing without rewriting an already accepted Held decision.

Use the actual Welcome/Reset CHUNK sequence as bootstrap context. The host's expected scope is the identifier it generated for that bootstrap, not a claim that a void transport callback delivered it. The client adopts a scope only after validating and applying the complete state. Old-scope proposals and feedback cannot steer the replacement timeline; rejoin binds the real peer.

Reuse the existing fine lead-control math with a bounded scale near 1 (approximately 0.98–1.02). Apply scale changes at the zero-delta ingress boundary used by the example, and keep it stable during its positive NORMAL call. Adapt the tested scale-aware offer/receipt calculations without reviving the abandoned TIMING1/INPUT2 checked-send and retirement feature stack. Preserve the eight-tick credit bound, exact offered debit, end limits and unresolved receipt quarantine. No wall clock enters simulation identity or admission.

An unavailable or deep deficit is explicit. Re-anchoring must run real bounded simulation/bootstrap or a validated Reset, never skip physics or input callbacks by assigning a head. Prediction8, ordinary repair8, H128 and the tracked64MiB limit remain unchanged.

Actions, proof and cleanup#

An input receipt acknowledges a proposal, not a unique gameplay outcome. Preserve original action identity and the actual accepted/rejected result. Do not turn a Held row into a second logical action. Any retry beyond existing packet redundancy needs an explicit stable identity, authority deduplication and outcome acknowledgement, with exactly-once effects across recovery.

The first actual pair completed tick300 with ten complete five-part comparisons, no recovery or missing decisions/effects, final acknowledgement and natural cleanup0. Normal Host FLOW samples were about40 KB per completed wire window; the last sampled counters showed one full bootstrap and96 signatures through tick288. These are short-run observations, not final-counter extrapolation or a600-second gate pass. The original report SHA is 5b2cd04d79e13eb9285fe8168def3c934af58df35821ffe5f81b63910018acc6. Its source/binary closure was secured before cleanup; old v1 and experimental results remain separate evidence.

After cleanup, the same focused groups and rebuilt SDK short pair passed. Runtime's actual size and requested/live Meter deltas are21,560 bytes per side, down from113,328 with the experimental observers. The cleaned primary impaired pair then completed610.0597 observed seconds through tick36,600 under the unchanged original policy:152/152 contested cycles,152 consecutive cycles, 1,220 complete state comparisons, no recovery or missing decisions/effects, final acknowledgement and natural cleanup0. Host emitted one full bootstrap and12,200 signatures; normal FLOW median output was40,802 bytes per wire window. The report SHA is 15f851a0e451161a0a3b4ebea3f0ca9efabab8c267b48dd255a2f9d20883906b; the coverage audit SHA is 007defa8445d647f194ecffdc4774ad32a3947ff0296ebda73e2deb7854a0626. This establishes that Kit primary impaired case, not the whole two-framework gate, cross-platform determinism or the affected CPU ceilings.

Prove signature-only confirmation, gap/mismatch/old-version rejection and full Reset recovery through public Session/Lane fixtures; then prove real Core/SDK input fidelity, full-five-part agreement, effects, ownership, budgets and the long matrix on the new wire identity. Historical v1 results remain historical.

After focused and real functional validation, remove superseded throttle experiments, temporary observers and unused prototype paths, retain useful regressions and evidence, and update documentation and builds. Audit usage before removing any shared Core capability. Certify Gate B on the cleaned graph.
